title: Nonempty separating open for pairs of norm sections
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $C$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral finite-type $F$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a finite group acting faithfully by $F$-automorphisms on $C$, meaning that $G\to\operatorname{Aut}_F(C)$ is injective. Let $L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Put $B=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*L$, and for a section $a$ of $L^{\otimes n}$ put $\mathcal N_G(a)=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*a$, a section of $B^{\otimes n}$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There is an integer $n_0\geq1$ such that for every $n\geq n_0$, writing $V_n=\Gamma(C,L^{\otimes n})$, there is a nonempty Zariski open $W_n\subseteq V_n\times V_n$. The finite-dimensional vector space $V_n\times V_n$ is regarded as an affine space over $F$ after any choice of basis. For every extension field $E/F$ and every $(a,b)\in W_n(E)$, the sections $\mathcal N_G(a),\mathcal N_G(b)$ generate $B_E^{\otimes n}$, and the induced morphism $[\mathcal N_G(a):\mathcal N_G(b)]:C_E\to\mathbf P^1_E$ is finite, surjective, $G$-invariant and etale on a nonempty open of $C_E$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections, def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. The symbols $C_E,L_E,B_E$ and $g_E$ denote scheme and module pullbacks along $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-module-pullback], and $\mathcal N_G$ on these sections uses the base-changed action. Nonemptiness is asserted as an $F$-scheme; $W_n(F)$ need not be nonempty if $F$ is finite. No condition on $\operatorname{char}F$ relative to $|G|$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/F$. The free-geometric-orbit lemma gives $D=C_\Omega$, $A=L_\Omega$ smooth proper integral with $A$ ample, and a rational point $x$ whose orbit $T=Gx$ has $|G|$ distinct points.

source.place: Assembly of the six statement-only arguments; original norm-pencil construction, returned steps 1–17. For invariance: constructions.tex Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space.

proof.text: Apply first-jet interpolation to this fixed $T$ and $x$. It gives one $n_0\geq1$ for all $n\geq n_0$, global generation of $A^{\otimes n}$, and a section $a$ with one simple zero at $x$ and coefficient $1$ at the other orbit points. Fix such an $n$.

source.place: Assembly of the six statement-only arguments; original norm-pencil construction, returned steps 1–17. For invariance: constructions.tex Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space.

proof.text: The geometric-witness lemma supplies $b$ whose norms $s,t$ generate $B_\Omega^{\otimes n}$ and satisfy $d(s/t)(x)\ne0$ in the chart $t\ne0$. This uses exactly one simple-zero factor, with no characteristic restriction.

source.place: Assembly of the six statement-only arguments; original norm-pencil construction, returned steps 1–17. For invariance: constructions.tex Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space.

proof.text: The universal-generation lemma gives finite-dimensional $V=\Gamma(C,L^{\otimes n})$, its scalar-extension identifications, polynomial universal norms on $P=V\times V$, and an open $U\subset P$ detecting generation over every extension field.

source.place: Assembly of the six statement-only arguments; original norm-pencil construction, returned steps 1–17. For invariance: constructions.tex Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space.

proof.text: Apply the differential-polynomial lemma with $M=B^{\otimes n}$ to those universal norms. It gives $\Delta:P\to\mathbf A(Q)$ and the open $D_\Delta$ detecting nonzero alternating differential after every extension. Set $W_n=U\cap D_\Delta$. The geometric pair above belongs to $U(\Omega)$ and its differential is nonzero at $x$, so belongs to $D_\Delta(\Omega)$. Thus $W_n$ is nonempty as an $F$-scheme.

source.place: Assembly of the six statement-only arguments; original norm-pencil construction, returned steps 1–17. For invariance: constructions.tex Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space.

proof.text: For any $E/F$ and $(a,b)\in W_n(E)$, its norms generate $M_E$ and have nonzero alternating differential. Apply the nonzero-pencil-differential lemma over $E$, since $C_E$ is smooth projective geometrically integral of dimension one, to obtain a finite surjective $h=[\mathcal N_G(a):\mathcal N_G(b)]$ etale on a nonempty open.

source.place: Assembly of the six statement-only arguments; original norm-pencil construction, returned steps 1–17. For invariance: constructions.tex Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space.

proof.text: The universal-norm lemma also identifies both pulled-back norm sections with their original sections under the single tensor-factor permutation $g\mapsto gk$, for each $k\in G$. Compatibility with pullback and equality for equivalent generating pairs give $h\circ k=h$. This holds over every $E$ and for every $n\geq n_0$, with no assertion that $W_n(F)$ is nonempty.
